note: One row per acceptance box. `blocker` says what stands between the box and being ticked, not how hard the code is. `asserted_by` names the test that would fail if the claim stopped holding; a box may not be ticked while it is null. `candidate_assertions` are tests that look like they might assert the box and have not been read. They deliberately do not satisfy the tick check.

rows.text: Installable user service, login startup and clean intentional shutdown.
Recovery after process failure, suspend/resume and loss of network access.
rows.asserted_by: Two of its three clauses. Process failure: tests/read_only.rs real_manager_recovers_disconnected_mount_after_process_death kills the mount process and asserts the manager reconnects, and real_manager_exits_with_client_handles_open covers the reverse. Loss of network access: the capacity fixtures' offline_remount phase remounts with the provider unreachable and asserts foreground_requests and content_reads both stay at zero, and tests/read_only.rs real_local_saves_remain_readable_during_upload_and_after_offline_restart covers the writable side.

rows.text: Real token expiry/refresh and visible reauthentication when consent expires.
rows.evidence: Partial: the installed daemon has refreshed its Microsoft grant hourly for 1.5 days without intervention (journal, 2026-09-07..09), which evidences real token refresh. Consent EXPIRY with visible reauthentication is a different event and unobserved.

rows.text: Responsive navigation during initial indexing and competing downloads.
rows.asserted_by: filesystem::capacity::real_combined_namespace_churn, churn.rs:403 -- read: asserts cached navigation stays under 500 ms while committed changes are being applied, on every round. Supported by content::windows::tests::graph::kernel fixtures covering navigation during a stalled transfer.

rows.text: Remove Graph metadata checks per cache block from the validated read-session fast path; implement and measure shared session setup, bounded sequential windows and safe renewal as specified in [read-session efficiency](adr/0004-read-session-efficiency.md).
rows.evidence: docs/validation.md#read-session-efficiency--measured-and-two-parts-not-exercised -- live 2026-09-09: shared setup measured (3 vs 13 Graph GETs, 271 vs 2166 ms, all samples matched). NOT exercised: conditional_windows=0 and renewals=0 in the run's own counters, so bounded sequential windows and safe renewal have no live evidence.

rows.text: Push-triggered metadata updates, reconnection/catch-up and periodic recovery checks, with provider delivery and local reaction latency measured separately.
rows.evidence: docs/validation.md#push-notifications--delivery-and-reaction-measured-separately -- live 2026-09-09: delivery 30.0/31.0/31.4 s, local reaction 287/169/174 ms, measured separately as the box requires. NOT covered live: reconnection, catch-up and periodic recovery, which remain synthetic only. One notification in seven live samples was never delivered (90 s deadline, 30 s typical); the pre-registered interference hypothesis was refuted by an immediately passing retry. Cause unexplained; the shipped 30 s poll bounds the impact.

rows.text: Bounded memory and background work with large libraries and long sessions.

Reclaim inactive namespace views with correct FUSE lifetimes; pass the 500,000-file traversal, invalidation and 24-hour churn memory gates in [namespace memory](adr/0005-namespace-memory.md). Content-cache limits do not satisfy this requirement.
Real restart/outage checks and at least 24 hours of sustained operation.
Provider-neutral create, update, rename, move and delete contracts (regular-file deletion; folder removal remains an explicit gap).
Durable local file contents and journal before local-save acknowledgement.
rows.asserted_by: tests/working_files.rs: killed_process_preserves_fsynced_save_and_newer_unsealed_changes -- read, not name-matched: after a SIGKILL it asserts the fsynced payload survives verbatim, the working file is still marked dirty, and the newer unsealed bytes are readable. Supported by queue_commit_and_working_generation_advance_are_one_transaction and partial_write_metadata_failure_recovers_actual_bytes_without_claiming_a_save.

rows.text: Persisted upload progress, resumable transfers and idempotent recovery.
rows.asserted_by: tests/upload_journal.rs: later_saves_follow_receipts_across_creation_upload_and_restart -- read: claim ordering survives restart, a second attempt keeps its id rather than duplicating, and its base resolves. With missing_receipt_precondition_never_falls_back_to_a_second_create, which asserts that an upload with no usable etag guard goes to Failed and keeps its payload rather than silently creating a duplicate. That pair is the idempotence claim.

rows.text: Version-conditional changes and preservation of both sides of conflicts.
rows.asserted_by: tests/upload_journal.rs: conflicted_predecessors_retain_newer_saves_and_allow_independent_work -- read: the conflicted item stays Pending with its newest local bytes intact while unrelated work proceeds, so neither side is discarded. With tests/causal_edits.rs: a_conflicted_rename_blocks_descendants_but_not_another_file.

rows.text: Distinct local-save, pending-upload, uploading, uploaded and failure states.
rows.asserted_by: tests/upload_journal.rs exercises every UploadState variant -- Pending, Uploading, Uploaded, Verifying, VerifyRequired, Conflict, Failed -- and asserts transitions between them, including that a failed upload retains its payload.

rows.text: Correct application save patterns, truncation and atomic replacement.
rows.evidence: docs/validation.md#writable-mount--real-application-saves -- live 2026-09-09: two direct saves (6.8/8.3 ms) and three atomic replacements including an online-only source after remount, old descriptor preserved, eight receipts, three conditional cleanups. NOT covered: in-place truncation -- the fixture calls truncate() at the size just written, so it is a no-op; generation 3 shrinks by replacement, not truncation.

rows.text: Crash/fault tests at every durable transition and concurrent remote edits.
rows.asserted_by: All 31 runtime durable transitions are crossed by a process that then dies, measured rather than read: each site records itself and each crash fixture persists what it reached. 30 are evidenced in a killed child; the preparation recovery in the process that opens the journal afterwards, because that is where recovery runs. See docs/benchmarks/durable-transition-sites.json.

rows.text: Opt-in write consent and live tests in a dedicated Cirrove test folder.
rows.asserted_by: cirrove-auth: write_consent_is_explicit_and_validates_granted_permissions; filesystem/writeback.rs refuses a mount whose account is not explicitly writable AND disabled, asserted by capacity::real_writable_namespace_retires_and_stays_bounded

rows.text: Persistent per-file and recursive-folder pinning with storage reservations.
Clear unpin/free-space behavior and accurate availability status.
Offline access and editing of pinned content, including across restart.
Unsent changes excluded from cache eviction and connection cleanup.
Disk-full recovery preserves edited data and explains required action.
Personal and business accounts, including multiple simultaneous accounts.
Explicit account, drive and SharePoint library selection.
Linked folders, duplicate links, moved/deleted links and folder-only access.
Per-item capabilities, restricted permissions and revoked-access behavior.
Remote creates, edits, moves and deletions update mounted views correctly.
Defined filename, package/notebook, trash and unsupported-operation behavior.
Documented compatibility matrix backed by real-account checks.
GTK4/libadwaita setup and settings without a terminal in ordinary flows.
Account picker, mount controls, reconnect, connection removal and cleanup.
Tray status and actions using the daemon as the source of truth.
Nautilus badges, pin/unpin actions and consistent status refresh.
Actionable errors, progress, cancellation and conflict resolution.
Keyboard navigation, accessibility, localization and visual verification.

Verify a declared session matrix covering native Wayland and X11, and GNOME and KDE Plasma: windows, dialogs, system dark-style preference and portal-backed folder opening, including cancellation and missing-portal behavior. Record the actual backend and supported session combinations; Xwayland is not native Wayland coverage. Current CI uses Xvfb (X11) only and does not exercise a complete GNOME or Plasma session.

One application identity across the desktop entry, installed application icon, AppStream metainfo, desktop application's D-Bus name and Wayland `app_id`. Verify launcher/window association, including X11, on every declared shell; naming consistency alone is not a runtime check.

Install application-specific scalable and symbolic icons in standard theme locations, replacing the generic application icon. Check dock, launcher and software-centre presentation, including symbolic recoloring.
Implement the tray as StatusNotifierItem over D-Bus. Document the GNOME extension requirement, detect missing tray support and keep all actions available from the window when no tray host is present.

Publish a supported file-manager list beyond the initial Nautilus target, with an explicit Dolphin decision and a shared daemon status contract behind each integration. Unsupported managers must still access mounted files; badge/control availability must be explained.

Preserve actionable, sanitized error causes in the window. Unreadable or invalid settings, an unreachable service and an incompatible service remain distinguishable, with recovery actions and diagnostic detail appropriate to the failure. Never expose credentials or raw provider responses.
Native Arch/AUR, Debian/Ubuntu `.deb` and Fedora `.rpm` packages from the same release, with the clean-system checks in [Distribution](distribution.md).
Signed APT and COPR update channels, release artifacts, source/provenance, supported-version matrix and measured reproducible build procedure.

Fresh installation through sign-in and reboot verified outside development. Validate this on each declared distribution family, including Fedora with SELinux enabled; an Ubuntu CI build is not an installation check.
Upgrade/migration rollback protects settings, credentials and pending work.
Clean uninstall and explicit retention/removal choices for local data.
User documentation, redacted diagnostics and supported-version policy.
Dependency/security review, extended testing and tracked release blockers.

Validate the desktop entry, installed icons and AppStream metainfo in CI, then compare their identity with the running window and application bus name in the supported desktop sessions. Current desktop-file validation alone does not satisfy this gate.

Build and install the daemon and CLI without GTK4/libadwaita present, with separate desktop packaging. The root's default members now exclude the desktop; explicit `--workspace` builds and full contributor checks still include it. A package installation on a clean headless host remains required; headless buildability does not imply unattended browser/keyring setup.
Tagged release and verified installation from the published artifacts.
